possibleCauses.name: Cold Draft / Airflow Shock
possibleCauses.explanation: Fiddle Leaf Figs react quickly to air conditioning vents or drafty doorways with localized brown spots and premature leaf shedding.

possibleCauses.name: Root Moisture Retention
possibleCauses.explanation: Watering every 5 days in low indirect light may keep the lower root ball perpetually saturated.

safeTreatments: Relocate plant at least 2 meters away from direct AC vents and heaters.
Allow top 5 cm (2 inches) of soil to dry before the next deep watering.
Wipe foliage with lukewarm water and ensure pot drains fully after each watering.
preventiveTips: Use a wooden chopstick or soil moisture probe before watering.
Rotate the pot a quarter turn each week to balance light reception.
healthReports.expertDisclaimer: This assessment is based on visual observations and reported environmental conditions. If leaf drop continues after adjusting airflow and moisture, consult a local botanical extension or plant nursery specialist.

diaryEntries.title: Wiped Monty’s foliage and checked aerial roots
diaryEntries.content: Gently cleaned dust from Monty’s large leaves with a damp microfiber cloth and lukewarm water. Directed two aerial roots into the soil to absorb extra moisture and stabilize the root ball.

diaryEntries.title: Tomatoes showing gorgeous color break!
diaryEntries.content: The first truss of Roma tomatoes has turned from pale orange to rich scarlet. Checked the leaves for any sign of blight or hornworms—everything looks spotless.

diaryEntries.title: Harvested fresh leaves for homemade pesto
diaryEntries.content: Pinched off about 40 grams of top basil leaves. Left the lower leaf pairs intact to trigger new lateral shoots. The fragrance filled the whole kitchen.

diaryEntries.title: Felix getting more indirect morning sunshine
diaryEntries.content: Moved Felix 50cm closer to the east-facing window away from the HVAC air vent. The leaves look perked up and less droopy after two weeks.
